expected_effect: Direction: lower public val_bpb. Size: EMA-weights public_val_bpb 0.002-0.006 below the same-host matched control (trn21 1.005734 or trn22 1.005967, whichever box runs it) and 0.002-0.006 below the raw-weights BPB logged in the same run. Predeclared thresholds: SUCCESS if EMA BPB <= control - 0.002 AND steps >= 2030 (trn21) / 2035 (trn22) (<=2% step loss). PARTIAL if EMA BPB < control by <0.002 with steps within 2%, or if EMA BPB <= control - 0.002 but steps are between the 2% and 10% bounds (1864-2029 on trn21, 1869-2034 on trn22; a win despite fewer steps is still evidence for EMA, but the throughput prediction failed and is recorded as such). FALSIFIED if EMA BPB >= raw BPB of the same run, or EMA BPB > control with steps within 2%. CONFOUNDED (protocol section 5) if steps < 1864 (trn21) / 1869 (trn22). Throughput hypothesis (not established fact): the per-step EMA update over all parameters including the BF16 n-gram tables (ledger: ngram_ve bf16=True) is expected to cost <2% of steps; if it costs more, that is recorded against the flag. public_val_bpb is the public development measurement; the official private-shard BPB shares the scoring function but not the data, so a public gain is a prediction about, not a measurement of, the official score. The paired raw-vs-EMA readout is the primary causal test because it shares one trajectory; the raw-weights BPB is expected to land within +/-0.002 of the control if the step count matches (sanity check that EMA is a pure shadow).
hypothesis: At the full 1800 s budget (~2071-2076 optimizer steps on the pinned controls), an exponential moving average of the in-run weights (decay 0.995, started at 75% of the budget, i.e. ~518 EMA updates) averages over roughly the final 200 low-learning-rate steps and yields lower public val_bpb than the raw final weights and than the matched same-host control. The documented 400 s negative result (train.py lines 293-297: decay 0.995, start_frac 0.75, BPB worsened by 0.0168) is explained by averaging lag, not by EMA being inert or harmful per se: at 400 s the run makes only ~460 steps, EMA is active for ~115 updates, and 0.995^115 = 0.56 of the evaluated EMA weight still sits on the stale step-~345 snapshot while the learning rate is still high. At 1800 s, 0.995^518 = 0.075 of the weight remains on the start snapshot, the effective window (~200 steps) is <10% of training, and it covers the low-LR tail where averaging reduces optimizer noise rather than trailing a fast-moving trajectory. Because train.py saves both raw and EMA weights and evaluates both (lines 301-305, 6223-6228), the same run provides a paired raw-vs-EMA comparison on one trajectory plus a comparison against the pinned control.
single_causal_change: Add --weight-ema only. Every other option stays at the 9a4caa7b defaults used by the two pinned controls (no precision, kernel, optimizer, schedule, or shape switch). --weight-ema-decay and --weight-ema-start-frac are not passed; both control ledger rows already record their resolved defaults as decays=(0.995,) start_frac=0.75 with weight_ema=False and updates=0, so the only behavioral delta is that EMA shadow weights are maintained after 75% of the budget, saved alongside the raw weights, and (per train.py 6223-6228) used as the preferred evaluation state when present.
